messages.content: It's extremely hot today and my air conditioner is currently turned off. Set it to start cooling at 20 degrees Celsius mid wind strength. power off after an hour

function.name: ThinQ_Connect
function.description: Sends a command to control an appliance, allowing only a single value to be sent in one call. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

body.description: A dictionary containing the parameters for the appliance command.

airConJobMode.description: The current job mode of the air conditioner.

windStrength.description: The strength of the air flow.

monitoringEnabled.description: Whether air quality sensor monitoring is enabled.

airCleanOperationMode.description: The operation mode for the air cleaning function.

airConOperationMode.description: The operation mode for the air conditioner, indicating if it is turned on or off.

powerSaveEnabled.description: Whether power save mode is enabled to conserve energy.

targetTemperature.description: The target temperature to set for the appliance, in degrees Celsius.

relativeHourToStop.description: The number of hours from the current time when the appliance should stop. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to stop.

relativeMinuteToStop.description: The number of minutes from the current time when the appliance should stop. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to stop.

relativeHourToStart.description: The number of hours from the current time when the appliance should start. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to start.

relativeMinuteToStart.description: The number of minutes from the current time when the appliance should start. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to start.

message.reasoning:
We need to parse user request: "It's extremely hot today and my air conditioner is currently turned off. Set it to start cooling at 20 degrees Celsius mid wind strength. power off after an hour"

We need to send a command via ThinQ_Connect. The body includes:

- airConJobMode: "COOL" (default is COOL, but we can specify)
- windStrength: "MID"
- airConOperationMode: "POWER_ON" (to start cooling)
- targetTemperature: 20
- relativeHourToStop: 1 (after an hour)
- relativeMinuteToStop: 0
- relativeHourToStart: 0? Actually we want to start immediately? The user says "Set it to start cooling at 20 degrees Celsius mid wind strength. power off after an hour". So we want to start now. So relativeHourToStart: 0, relativeMinuteToStart: 0? Or maybe we don't need to set start times; we just set operation mode to POWER_ON. But the function expects relativeHourToStart and relativeMinuteToStart. They default to null. If we want to start now, we can set them to 0? But the function may interpret 0 as immediate? The spec says "number of hours from the current time when the appliance should start. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to start." So if we set to null, it won't schedule to start. But we want to start now. We can set relativeHourToStart: 0, relativeMinuteToStart: 0. That might schedule to start now. Alternatively, we can leave them null and set airConOperationMode to POWER_ON. That might start immediately. But the spec says "airConOperationMode: indicates if it is turned on or off." So setting to POWER_ON should start it. So we don't need to set start times. So we can set relativeHourToStart: null, relativeMinuteToStart: null.

Thus body:

{
  airConJobMode: "COOL",
  windStrength: "MID",
  airConOperationMode: "POWER_ON",
  targetTemperature: 20,
  relativeHourToStop: 1,
  relativeMinuteToStop: 0,
  relativeHourToStart: null,
  relativeMinuteToStart: null
}

We also might want to set monitoringEnabled: false, powerSaveEnabled: false, etc. But defaults are fine.

Thus we call ThinQ_Connect with body.

We need to produce JSON. The function call format: 
{
  "name": "ThinQ_Connect",
  "arguments": {
    "body": { ... }
  }
}

We need to output that.
